tokens, such as :arg0. Unlike other translation-based models, we do not add predicates (e.g., have-condition-91) into the vocabulary because they have ingorable effects on performance according to our preliminary experiments.

We train our models for 50,000 steps, using a batch size of 16. This amounts to approximately 22 epochs on AMR 2.0 and around 15 epochs on AMR 3.0. We use an AdamW optimizer (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2019), accompanied by a cosine learning rate scheduler (Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017) with a warm-up phase of 5,000 steps. The peak learning rate is set at $5 \times 10^{-5}$ for base models and $3 \times 10^{-5}$ for large models.
